Neither real nor illusory faces caused interference: 'Neither the main effect of Distractor type, F(2,58) = 1.70, p = .19, nor the interaction between the two factors, F < 1, was significant.' Bayesian analysis provided moderate evidence against Distractor type (BF_incl = 0.17).

description: Professional and amateur musicians have younger-appearing brains than non-musicians as measured by Brain Age Gap Estimation (BrainAGE), with both groups showing approximately 4 years younger estimated brain age than healthy controls
original_authors: Lars Rogenmoser; Julius Kernbach; Gottfried Schlaug; Christian Gaser
original_title: Keeping brains young with making music
replication_authors: Anna Maria Matziorinis; Christian Gaser; Stefan Koelsch
replication_title: Is musical engagement enough to keep the brain young?
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'The study failed to replicate the findings from a previous BrainAGE and music-making study (Rogenmoser et al. 2018) revealing no association between musician status and BrainAGE scores.' The t-test comparing non-musicians and amateur-musicians was non-significant (t(123) = 1.20, p = 0.23).

description: Genetic linkage to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) at chromosomal region 4p16 in European American multiplex families, identified by Haseman-Elston regression multipoint model-free linkage analysis
original_authors: Gray-McGuire C.; Moser KL; Gaffney PM; Kelly J.; Yu H.; Olson JM; Jedrey CM; Jacobs KB; Kimberly RP; Neas BR; Rich SS; Behrens TW; Harley JB
original_title: Genome scan of human systemic lupus erythematosus by regression modeling: evidence of linkage and epistasis at 4p16-15.2
replication_authors: Chao Xing; Andrea L. Sestak; Jennifer A. Kelly; Kim L. Nguyen; Gail R. Bruner; John B. Harley; Courtney Gray-McGuire
replication_title: Localization and replication of the systemic lupus erythematosus linkage signal at 4p16: interaction with 2p11, 12q24 and 19q13 in European Americans
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'In the present study we replicate this linkage effect in a new cohort of 76 EA families multiplex for SLE by model-free linkage analysis.' The replication achieved P = 4.7 × 10⁻³ in the new cohort using the same Haseman-Elston regression approach, and the Discussion confirms 'we tested this hypothesis in a new collection of EA pedigrees, and replicated the linkage signal at 4p16.'

description: Variants in the ChAT (choline acetyltransferase) gene are associated with nicotine dependence in European American smokers
original_authors: Ray R.; Mitra N.; Baldwin D.; Guo M.; Patterson F.; Heitjan DF; Jepson C.; Wileyto EP; Wei J.; Payne T.; Ma JZ; Li MD; Lerman C.
original_title: Convergent evidence that choline acetyltransferase gene variation is associated with prospective smoking cessation and nicotine dependence
replication_authors: Jinxue Wei; Jennie Z. Ma; Thomas J. Payne; Wenyan Cui; Riju Ray; Nandita Mitra; Caryn Lerman; Ming D. Li
replication_title: Replication and extension of association of choline acetyltransferase with nicotine dependence in European and African American smokers
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'our individual SNP- and haplotype-based association analyses revealed that ChAT is associated with ND in both the AA and EA samples, which represents not only a replication of previous association reports in EA populations, but also an extension to an independent ethnic population.' Significant haplotype associations with all three nicotine dependence measures were found in both the EA and AA samples, all surviving Bonferroni correction.

description: The genetic effects of ADH1B and ADH1C regions on the risk of alcohol dependence derive from the ADH1B*47Arg/*47Arg genotype (rs1229984, H47R), and positive association signals from other sites in ADH1B and ADH1C track this single variant rather than representing independent effects
original_authors: Ihn-Geun Choi; Hyun-Gyun Son; Byung-Hwan Yang; Seok Hyeon Kim; Jun-Suk Lee; Young-Gyu Chai; Bong Ki Son; Baik Seok Kee; Byung Lae Park; Lyoung Hyo Kim; Yoo Hyun Choi; Hyoung Doo Shin
original_title: Scanning of genetic effects of alcohol metabolism gene (ADH1B and ADH1C) polymorphisms on the risk of alcoholism
replication_authors: Byung Lae Park; Jee Wook Kim; Hyun Sub Cheong; Lyoung Hyo Kim; Boung Chul Lee; Cheong Hoon Seo; Tae-Cheon Kang; Young-Woo Nam; Goon-Bo Kim; Hyoung Doo Shin; Ihn-Geun Choi
replication_title: Extended genetic effects of ADH cluster genes on the risk of alcohol dependence: from GWAS to replication
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'When the SNPs in the ADH gene cluster were conditionally analyzed by controlling for odds ratios derived from referent analysis of ADH1B rs1229984 (H47R), all positive signals disappeared, as consistent with our previous study (Table 3).' They further conclude: 'These results confirmed and expanded our previous findings, indicating that ADH1B rs1229984 (H47R) might be a sole genetic marker tracking the genetic effects of the risk of AD in the ADH gene cluster region.'

description: Increased CON1 copy number of DUF1220 protein domains is linearly associated with increasing severity of social impairment (ADI-R Social Diagnostic Score) in individuals with autism
original_authors: Jonathan M. Davis; Veronica B. Searles; Nathan Anderson; Jonathon Keeney; Laura Dumas; James M. Sikela
original_title: DUF1220 dosage is linearly associated with increasing severity of the three primary symptoms of autism
replication_authors: Davis JM; Searles Quick VB; Sikela JM
replication_title: Replicated linear association between DUF1220 copy number and severity of social impairment in autism
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'This report presents a replication of our previous study demonstrating a linear association between CON1 copy number and progressively more impaired Social Diagnostic Score as measured by the ADI-R.' The replication found β=0.24 (p=0.036), virtually identical to the original β=0.25 (p=0.021).

description: Increased CON1 copy number of DUF1220 protein domains is linearly associated with increasing severity of communicative impairment (ADI-R Verbal Communication Diagnostic Score) in individuals with autism
original_authors: Jonathan M. Davis; Veronica B. Searles; Nathan Anderson; Jonathon Keeney; Laura Dumas; James M. Sikela
original_title: DUF1220 dosage is linearly associated with increasing severity of the three primary symptoms of autism
replication_authors: Davis JM; Searles Quick VB; Sikela JM
replication_title: Replicated linear association between DUF1220 copy number and severity of social impairment in autism
explanation: The authors report 'an analogous trend between CON1 copy number and Communicative Diagnostic Score' but the effect did not reach statistical significance (β=0.16, p=0.072). The Discussion notes the beta values are 'highly similar with similar standard errors' to the original (β=0.18, p=0.030), suggesting a partial/trending replication.

description: Increased CON1 copy number of DUF1220 protein domains is linearly associated with increasing severity of repetitive behaviors (ADI-R Repetitive Behavior Diagnostic Score) in individuals with autism
original_authors: Jonathan M. Davis; Veronica B. Searles; Nathan Anderson; Jonathon Keeney; Laura Dumas; James M. Sikela
original_title: DUF1220 dosage is linearly associated with increasing severity of the three primary symptoms of autism
replication_authors: Davis JM; Searles Quick VB; Sikela JM
replication_title: Replicated linear association between DUF1220 copy number and severity of social impairment in autism
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'The association originally identified between CON1 and repetitive behaviors in the previous study was not replicated here.' The replication found β=0.00 (p=1.0) compared to the original β=0.10 (p=0.047).

description: Variants in the RELN gene (rs39395 on chromosome 7q22.1) are associated with otosclerosis in case-control populations from Belgium, Holland, and France
original_authors: Isabelle Schrauwen; Megan Ealy; Matthew J. Huentelman; Melissa Thys; Nils Homer; Kathleen Vanderstraeten; Erik Fransen; Jason J. Corneveaux; David W. Craig; Mireille Claustres; Cor W.R.J. Cremers; Ingeborg Dhooge; Paul Van de Heyning; Robert Vincent; Erwin Offeciers; Richard J.H. Smith; Guy Van Camp
original_title: A genome-wide analysis identifies genetic variants in the RELN gene associated with otosclerosis
replication_authors: Andrew J. Mowat; Michael Crompton; Joanna L. Ziff; Christopher P. Aldren; Jeremy A. Lavy; Shakeel R. Saeed; Sally J. Dawson
replication_title: Evidence of distinct RELN and TGFB1 genetic associations in familial and non-familial otosclerosis in a British population
explanation: The whole-cohort analysis found no significant association between any of the three RELN SNPs and otosclerosis (all p>0.3), failing to replicate the original GWAS finding. However, a significant association (p=0.0057) was detected for rs39399 in familial otosclerosis cases only, suggesting a subgroup-dependent effect. The authors conclude that 'our results suggest that an association exists between rs39399 and the familial form of otosclerosis, which requires further investigation.'

description: The rs1800472 coding polymorphism (T263I) in TGFB1 is associated with otosclerosis in Belgian-Dutch and French populations
original_authors: Melissa Thys; Isabelle Schrauwen; Kathleen Vanderstraeten; Katrien Janssens; Nele Dieltjens; Kris Van Den Bogaert; Erik Fransen; Wenjie Chen; Megan Ealy; Mireille Claustres; Cor R.W.J. Cremers; Ingeborg Dhooge; Frank Declau; Jos Claes; Paul Van de Heyning; Robert Vincent; Thomas Somers; Erwin Offeciers; Richard J.H. Smith; Guy Van Camp
original_title: The coding polymorphism T263I in TGF-beta1 is associated with otosclerosis in two independent populations
replication_authors: Andrew J. Mowat; Michael Crompton; Joanna L. Ziff; Christopher P. Aldren; Jeremy A. Lavy; Shakeel R. Saeed; Sally J. Dawson
replication_title: Evidence of distinct RELN and TGFB1 genetic associations in familial and non-familial otosclerosis in a British population
explanation: The study found a significant association between rs1800472 in TGFB1 and otosclerosis (p=0.021 in the whole cohort; p=0.015 in non-familial cases). The conclusion explicitly states: 'This replicates two previous studies which have found the same association in the same direction,' and the authors note the association was confirmed in the same direction as the original (major allele protective).

description: Four paired swallowing events (AEstart before Pop, Pop before/with BP1, HL after Pop, PAmax after PESmax) always occur in a stereotyped obligatory order during healthy pharyngeal swallowing, and a single most common overall event sequence (AEclose → Pop ≤ BP1 → H2 → PESmax → HL → PAmax) characterizes healthy swallowing
original_authors: Katherine A. Kendall; Rebecca J. Leonard; Susan W. McKenzie
original_title: Sequence variability during hypopharyngeal bolus transit
replication_authors: Sonja M. Molfenter; Chelsea Leigh; Catriona M. Steele
replication_title: Event Sequence Variability in Healthy Swallowing: Building on Previous Findings
explanation: The authors explicitly conclude they concurred with two of the four obligatory paired-event sequences (AEstart before Pop and HL after Pop) but 'failed to replicate the previous findings that there is obligatory sequencing of maximum pharyngeal constriction after maximal UES distension and the UES opens before bolus arrival at the UES.' The most common overall sequence was observed in only 4/293 (1.3%) swallows versus 25% in the original. Thus the replication produced mixed results — partial success and partial failure.

description: EUS nodal status (N-stage and N0 vs N+) is an independent predictor of overall survival in oesophageal cancer patients staged N0 with PET/CT
original_authors: Foley KG; Lewis WG; Fielding P.; Karran A.; Chan D.; Blake P.; Roberts SA
original_title: N-staging of oesophageal and junctional carcinoma: is there still a role for EUS in patients staged N0 at PET/CT?
replication_authors: Foley KG; Fielding P.; Lewis WG; Roberts SA
replication_title: Additional value of EUS in oesophageal cancer patients staged N0 on PET/CT: validation of a prognostic model
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the conclusion: 'This validation study did not replicate the results of the developed prognostic model.' In the validation cohort, EUS N-stage (p = 0.553) and EUS N0 versus N+ (p = 0.359) were not significantly associated with overall survival in multivariate analysis, contrary to the original study's findings.

description: Foodservice interventions (including oral nutrition support) improve nutritional outcomes and satisfaction of adult oncology patients in hospital and ambulatory settings
original_authors: Elizabeth Doyle; Natalie Simmance; Helen Wilding; Judi Porter
original_title: Systematic review and meta-analyses of foodservice interventions and their effect on nutritional outcomes and satisfaction of adult oncology patients
replication_authors: Belinda Steer; Jacqueline Black; Laura Cecchini; Clarissa Choo; Ana Dvarakesa; Martha Hill; Athena Ho; Georgia Kennett; Andre Woltersdorf; Emily Zilber; Judi Porter
replication_title: Foodservice interventions and their influence on nutritional outcomes and satisfaction of adult oncology patients—a conceptual replication
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a conceptual replication of Doyle et al. (2017) and conclude: 'This conceptual replication found that the implementation of small, frequent high-energy high-protein meals and snacks and patient-focused foodservice models was found to improve a number of nutritional outcomes in both inpatient and ambulatory settings,' confirming the positive direction of the original review's findings.

description: Children living in more deprived neighbourhoods show a widening mental health gap compared to less deprived peers as they age from 4 to 7 years (amplification of social differences in child mental health over time)
original_authors: Louise Marryat; Lucy Thompson; Helen Minnis; Philip Wilson
original_title: Primary schools and the amplification of social differences in child mental health: a population-based cohort study
original_journal: Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health
replication_authors: Katie Finning; Amy Haeffner; Sohum Patel; Bryony Longdon; Rachel Hayes; Obioha C. Ukoumunne; Tamsin Ford
replication_title: Is neighbourhood deprivation in primary school-aged children associated with their mental health and does this association change over 30 months?
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'We failed to replicate the widening of the disparity in mental health by socioeconomic deprivation with age that was reported by Marryat et al. [7].' Tests of interaction between IMD quintile and year group at baseline were not significant for teacher- or parent-reported SDQ total difficulties scores, though the general association between deprivation and worse mental health was confirmed.

description: Greater developmental telomere attrition (telomere shortening during development) predicts greater impulsivity in adult European starlings, as measured by adjusting-delay procedure
original_authors: Melissa Bateson; Ben O. Brilot; Robert Gillespie; Pat Monaghan; Daniel Nettle
original_title: Developmental telomere attrition predicts impulsive decision-making in adult starlings
original_journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
replication_authors: Jonathon Dunn; Clare Andrews; Daniel Nettle; Melissa Bateson
replication_title: Developmental history, energetic state and choice impulsivity in European starlings, Sturnus vulgaris
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'We did not replicate the findings from Bateson et al. (2015) that greater developmental telomere attrition predicts greater impulsivity in adulthood.' Model 1 (N=25) found no significant effect of ΔTL on impulsivity (LRT=0.08, p=0.78).

description: Lower body condition (mass for skeletal size) predicts greater impulsivity in adult European starlings
original_authors: Melissa Bateson; Ben O. Brilot; Robert Gillespie; Pat Monaghan; Daniel Nettle
original_title: Developmental telomere attrition predicts impulsive decision-making in adult starlings
original_journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
replication_authors: Jonathon Dunn; Clare Andrews; Daniel Nettle; Melissa Bateson
replication_title: Developmental history, energetic state and choice impulsivity in European starlings, Sturnus vulgaris
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Discussion: 'We did not replicate the findings from Bateson et al. (2015) that...lower energetic reserves overall, as measured by lower body condition, predicts greater impulsivity.' Model 1 (N=25) found no significant effect of body condition on impulsivity (LRT=0.02, p=0.90).

description: The midbrain-to-pons ratio calculated from conventional brain MRI has high specificity and sensitivity for diagnosing progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), with all non-PSP subjects having ratios higher than 0.52 and most neuropathologically confirmed PSP patients having ratios lower than 0.52
original_authors: Luke A. Massey; Hans R. Jäger; Dominic C. Paviour; Sean S. O'Sullivan; Helen Ling; David R. Williams; Constantinos Kallis; Janice Holton; Tamas Revesz; David J. Burn; Tarek Yousry; Andrew J. Lees; Nick C. Fox; Caroline Micallef
original_title: The midbrain to pons ratio: a simple and specific MRI sign of progressive supranuclear palsy
replication_authors: Valtteri Kaasinen; Noora Kangassalo; Maria Gardberg; Juuso Isotalo; Jari Karhu; Riitta Parkkola; Pirkko Sonninen
replication_title: Midbrain-to-pons ratio in autopsy-confirmed progressive supranuclear palsy: replication in an independent cohort
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we replicated both the 100% specificity and the suboptimal sensitivity of the ratio measurement' and conclude that midbrain-to-pons ratios constitute 'reliable and clinically useful estimates of diagnostic midbrain atrophy in relation to PSP pathology.' The replication found PSP patients had clearly lower ratios than non-PSP patients (p < 0.0001), with 100% PPV and 95.8% NPV.

description: Citizens in six European countries are willing to pay approximately €21.80 per household per month (median €10.00) for an integrated, international early warning system for infectious diseases
original_authors: Sebastian Himmler; Job van Exel; Meg Perry-Duxbury; Werner Brouwer
original_title: Willingness to pay for an early warning system for infectious diseases
replication_authors: Sebastian Himmler; Job van Exel; Werner Brouwer
replication_title: Did the COVID-19 pandemic change the willingness to pay for an early warning system for infectious diseases in Europe?
replication_journal: The European Journal of Health Economics
explanation: The replication found significantly higher WTP in 2020 vs 2018 (mean ~50% increase, e.g., €20 to €28 in the 'System' scenario), but the phenomenon of positive WTP for the early warning system was confirmed. The authors conclude: 'we found a higher WTP in 2020 as compared to 2018 in all countries except Hungary,' indicating the original magnitude did not replicate exactly while the effect direction remained consistent.

description: Higher numbers of syndemic psychosocial health conditions are additively associated with greater sexual risk behavior and higher HIV prevalence among men who have sex with men, with a falloff in HIV infection at the highest levels of syndemic burden
original_authors: Ron Stall; Thomas C. Mills; John Williamson; Trevor Hart; Greg Greenwood; Jay Paul; Lance Pollack; Diane Binson; Dennis Osmond; Joseph A. Catania
original_title: Association of cooccurring psychosocial health problems and increased vulnerability to HIV/AIDS among urban men who have sex with men
replication_authors: Ann O’Leary; John B. Jemmott; Robin Stevens; Scott Edward Rutledge; Larry D. Icard
replication_title: Optimism and Education Buffer the Effects of Syndemic Conditions on HIV Status Among African American Men Who Have Sex with Men
explanation: The authors explicitly state in the Conclusions: 'Results of the present study replicate previous findings that syndemic burden is associated with elevated levels of HIV sexual risk behavior and likelihood of HIV infection among black MSM. We also replicated the findings of Stall et al. [5] that, at higher levels of syndemic burden, likelihood of HIV infection drops off.' The replication is classified as 'close extension' because it uses the same syndemic paradigm but applies it specifically to African American MSM, testing generalizability to a different racial/ethnic subpopulation.

description: Choosing an upcoming emotional situation (situation selection) decreases negative experience, reduces exocrine and respiratory arousal, and enhances expressivity in negative viewing, while leaving positive experience unaffected
original_authors: Simon Thuillard; Elise S. Dan-Glauser
original_title: The regulatory effect of choice in situation selection reduces experiential, exocrine and respiratory arousal for negative emotional stimulations
replication_authors: Simon Thuillard; Elise S. Dan-Glauser
replication_title: Efficiency of Illusory Choice Used as a Variant of Situation Selection for Regulating Emotions: Reduction of Positive Experience But Preservation of Physiological Downregulation
explanation: The authors state 'By mostly replicating the results that presented Situation selection as an efficient emotion regulation strategy' — they confirmed the decrease in negative experience, the physiological effects (skin conductance, respiratory amplitude, heart rate orienting response), and the absence of effect on positive experience, but explicitly noted they 'did not find the previously reported expressivity enhancement in negative viewing,' indicating a partial rather than full replication.

description: Item triangulation across in-school, in-home, and parental questionnaires can identify inaccurate responders and jokesters in adolescent survey data, and their inclusion exaggerates health disparities for small subgroups such as adoptees
original_authors: Xitao Fan; Brent C. Miller; Kyung-Eun Park; Bryan W. Winward; Mathew Christensen; Harold D. Grotevant; Robert H. Tai
original_title: An exploratory study about inaccuracy and invalidity in adolescent self-report surveys
replication_authors: Jessica N. Fish; Stephen T. Russell
replication_title: Have Mischievous Responders Misidentified Sexual Minority Youth Disparities in the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health?
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'In our first approach, we replicated the original item triangulation of in-school, in-home, and parental questionnaires developed by Fan et al. (2006) to identify inaccurate responders and jokesters.' The triangulation method was successfully applied to Add Health data, identifying a similar proportion of inaccurate responders and jokesters (1.24% and 0.17%, respectively, compared to Fan et al.'s ~1.62% and ~0.39%), confirming the method works as expected.

description: Wave 1 same-sex attracted males who later reported heterosexual identities in adulthood (especially males) were more likely to be jokesters or mischievous responders, and their inclusion exaggerates sexual minority health disparities in Add Health data
original_authors: Ritch C. Savin-Williams; Kara Joyner
original_title: The dubious assessment of gay, lesbian, and bisexual adolescents of add health
replication_authors: Jessica N. Fish; Stephen T. Russell
replication_title: Have Mischievous Responders Misidentified Sexual Minority Youth Disparities in the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health?
explanation: The authors replicated the analytical sample used by Savin-Williams and Joyner (2014a) and found no evidence supporting their claims: 'Participants who reported Wave 1 same-sex attraction and Wave 4 heterosexual identities were no more likely to fall into inaccurate responder or jokester categories' (p = .912 for males, p = .876 for females). The authors conclude: 'Our results show that this conclusion is misleading.'

description: Mischievous responding among LGBQ youth in school-based surveys substantially biases estimates of health disparities between sexual minority and heterosexual youth, with 11.7% of LGBQ adolescents flagged for three or more low-frequency responses
original_authors: Joseph P. Robinson-Cimpian
original_title: Inaccurate estimation of disparities due to mischievous responders: Several suggestions to assess conclusions
replication_authors: Jessica N. Fish; Stephen T. Russell
replication_title: Have Mischievous Responders Misidentified Sexual Minority Youth Disparities in the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health?
explanation: Reviewer upgrade to high: The authors applied Robinson-Cimpian's (2014) mischievous index methodology to Add Health data and found dramatically lower rates of mischievous responding among sexual minority youth (1.3-3.4% vs. Robinson-Cimpian's 11.7% for 3+ low-frequency responses). Controlling for mischievousness eliminated only 1 of 7 established health disparities (suicidal ideation for both-sex attracted males); 6 disparities survived and some actually increased. The authors conclude unambiguously: 'We found little evidence of inaccurate responders or mischief among same-sex attracted youth and, with one exception, we found that controlling for mischievous responses did not change results for sexual minority disparities.' Classification as 'close extension' is correct because the same methodology was applied in a different survey context (in-home interview vs. school-based SAQ).

description: Adolescents with greater exposure to sexually dominant behavior in pornography are more likely to engage in sexually dominant behavior, which in turn is associated with lower partnered sexual satisfaction (mediation pathway: pornography exposure → sexually dominant behavior → lower sexual satisfaction)
original_authors: Paul J. Wright; Debby Herbenick; Bryant Paul; Robert S. Tokunaga
original_title: Exploratory findings on U.S. adolescents' pornography use, dominant behavior, and sexual satisfaction
replication_authors: Paul J. Wright; Debby Herbenick; Robert S. Tokunaga
replication_title: Adolescents’ Pornography Exposure, Sexually Dominant Behavior, and Partnered Sexual Satisfaction: Replication in a U.S. Probability Sample
explanation: The authors found mixed results across the three paths in the mediation model. The sexually dominant behavior → sexual satisfaction path achieved full replication (both significant, CIs overlapping), but the pornography exposure → sexually dominant behavior path and the indirect (mediation) effect both achieved only semi-partial replication. The indirect effect was not statistically significant in the replication (b = -0.03, p = .15) though it overlapped with the lower bound of the original's 95% CI. The authors conclude: 'findings from Wright et al. (2021) and the present study are suggestive of a mediational linkage between these variables, but larger samples and longitudinal designs are required to rigorously substantiate this hypothesis.'

description: GABRA2 SNP rs279871 is associated with adolescent conduct disorder (CD) in a clinical sample of youth with substance use and conduct problems
original_authors: Joseph T. Sakai; Michael C. Stallings; Thomas J. Crowley; Heather L. Gelhorn; Matthew B. McQueen; Marissa A. Ehringer
original_title: Test of association between GABRA2 (SNP rs279871) and adolescent conduct/alcohol use disorders utilizing a sample of clinic referred youth with serious substance and conduct problems, controls and available first degree relatives
replication_authors: Whitney E. Melroy; Sarah H. Stephens; Joseph T. Sakai; Helen M. Kamens; Matthew B. McQueen; Robin P. Corley; Michael C. Stallings; Christian J. Hopfer; Kenneth S. Krauter; Sandra A. Brown; John K. Hewitt; Marissa A. Ehringer
replication_title: Examination of Genetic Variation in GABRA2 with Conduct Disorder and Alcohol Abuse and Dependence in a Longitudinal Study
explanation: The authors explicitly state this study was 'designed as a replication and extension of the Sakai et al. (2010) study.' In the conclusion, they state: 'we did not replicate previous findings showing associations between rs279871 and rs279858 with adolescent CD and adult AAD.' The two well-replicated GABRA2 SNPs (rs279858 and rs279871) showed no significant associations with CD or alcohol dependence.

description: Additive-genetic variance in IQ increases with family socioeconomic status (A×SES effect) in young children
original_authors: Turkheimer, Eric; Haley, Andreana; Waldron, Mary; D'Onofrio, Brian; Gottesman, Irving I.
original_title: Socioeconomic status modifies heritability of IQ in young children
replication_authors: Robert M. Kirkpatrick; Matt McGue; William G. Iacono
replication_title: Replication of a Gene–Environment Interaction Via Multimodel Inference: Additive-Genetic Variance in Adolescents’ General Cognitive Ability Increases with Family-of-Origin Socioeconomic Status
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'we replicated only the A×SES effect of Turkheimer et al. (2003): additive-genetic variance varied positively with family SES' with p = 0.0019, surviving even Bonferroni correction. The effect was robust to model specification.

description: Shared-environmental variance in IQ decreases with family socioeconomic status (C×SES effect) in young children
original_authors: Turkheimer, Eric; Haley, Andreana; Waldron, Mary; D'Onofrio, Brian; Gottesman, Irving I.
original_title: Socioeconomic status modifies heritability of IQ in young children
replication_authors: Robert M. Kirkpatrick; Matt McGue; William G. Iacono
replication_title: Replication of a Gene–Environment Interaction Via Multimodel Inference: Additive-Genetic Variance in Adolescents’ General Cognitive Ability Increases with Family-of-Origin Socioeconomic Status
explanation: The authors explicitly state that 'The C×SES effect was not in the hypothesized direction and was estimated with little statistical precision' (p = 0.5307), and found 'none for the hypothesized C×SES effect.'

description: The -493G/T MTP variant (rs2866164) is associated with human longevity, with the minor G allele depleted in centenarians compared to controls
original_authors: Bard J. Geesaman; Erica Benson; Stephanie J. Brewster; Louis M. Kunkel; Hélène Blanché; Gilles Thomas; Thomas T. Perls; Mark J. Daly; Annibale A. Puca
original_title: Haplotype-based identification of a microsomal transfer protein marker associated with the human lifespan
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
replication_authors: Valeria Novelli; Chiara Viviani Anselmi; Roberta Roncarati; Guia Guffanti; Alberto Malovini; Giulio Piluso; Annibale Alessandro Puca
replication_title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity
explanation: The authors report that after adding 156 additional controls, 'By including these controls the association disappeared.' The Discussion confirms '-493G/T MTP (rs2866164) showed no associations with exceptional longevity.'

description: The homozygous GG genotype of CETP I405V polymorphism (rs5882) is enriched in centenarians and centenarian offspring, and is associated with exceptional longevity in Ashkenazi-Jewish populations
original_authors: N. Barzilai; G. Atzmon; C. Schechter; E. Schaefer; A. Cupples; R. Lipton; Suzanne Cheng; A. Shuldiner
original_title: Unique lipoprotein phenotype and genotype associated with exceptional longevity
replication_authors: Valeria Novelli; Chiara Viviani Anselmi; Roberta Roncarati; Guia Guffanti; Alberto Malovini; Giulio Piluso; Annibale Alessandro Puca
replication_title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity
explanation: The authors state: 'The homozygous GG (that corresponds to VV) for CETP I405V (rs5882) shows no differences in frequency among cases and controls (Table 5). This is contrary to the original data published (Arai et al. 2000), but is in accordance with a subsequent attempt to reproduce the results in Italian populations.' The Discussion confirms CETP I405V 'showed no associations with exceptional longevity.'

description: The heterozygous Klotho KL-VS variant (rs952706) is enriched in the elderly (protective effect) while the homozygous form is depleted (detrimental effect), associating with exceptional human longevity
original_authors: Dan E. Arking; Alice Krebsová; Milan Maçek; Milan Maçek; Albert Arking; Shahzad I. Mian; Linda F. Fried; Ada Hamosh; Srabani Dey; Iain McIntosh; Harry C. Dietz
original_title: Association of human aging with a functional variant of klotho
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
replication_authors: Valeria Novelli; Chiara Viviani Anselmi; Roberta Roncarati; Guia Guffanti; Alberto Malovini; Giulio Piluso; Annibale Alessandro Puca
replication_title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity
explanation: The authors report that 'KL-VS variant (rs952706) showed the same distributions of allele and genotype frequencies between cases and controls (Table 5), not supporting previous reports.' The Discussion confirms 'Klotho KL-VS variant (rs952706)... showed no associations with exceptional longevity.'

description: APOC3 -641CC genotypes are more frequent among long-living Ashkenazi-Jewish individuals, and CC carriers had lower prevalence of hypertension and greater insulin sensitivity
original_authors: Gil Atzmon; Marielisa Rincon; Clyde B. Schechter; Alan R. Shuldiner; Richard B. Lipton; Aviv Bergman; Nir Barzilai
original_title: Lipoprotein genotype and conserved pathway for exceptional longevity in humans
replication_authors: Valeria Novelli; Chiara Viviani Anselmi; Roberta Roncarati; Guia Guffanti; Alberto Malovini; Giulio Piluso; Annibale Alessandro Puca
replication_title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity
explanation: The authors report that 'APOC3 -641C/A (rs2542052) showed the same distributions of allele and genotype frequencies between cases and controls (Table 5), not supporting previous reports.' The Discussion confirms '-641C/A APOC3 (rs2542052)... showed no associations with exceptional longevity.'

description: The Q192R variant of PON1 (rs662) shows a controversial association with longevity, with differing reports on whether the variant is protective or detrimental in centenarian populations
original_authors: Irene M. Rea; Pascal P. McKeown; Dorothy McMaster; Ian S. Young; Chris Patterson; Maurice J. Savage; Christine Belton; Francesca Marchegiani; Fabiola Olivieri; Massimiliano Bonafe; Claudio Franceschi
original_title: Paraoxonase polymorphisms PON1 192 and 55 and longevity in Italian centenarians and Irish nonagenarians. A pooled analysis
replication_authors: Valeria Novelli; Chiara Viviani Anselmi; Roberta Roncarati; Guia Guffanti; Alberto Malovini; Giulio Piluso; Annibale Alessandro Puca
replication_title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity
explanation: Reviewer verified: The replication result is unambiguous failure despite the original finding being described as 'controversial.' Table 5 shows all PON1 p-values are deeply non-significant (genotype p=0.477/0.933/0.849; allele p=0.861/0.816/0.814) with odds ratios ~1.0 (1.0, 0.97, 0.97) across two independent LLI groups and combined. The Results section explicitly states PON1 Q192R 'showed the same distributions of allele and genotype frequencies between cases and controls, not supporting previous reports.' The Discussion confirms 'PON1 Q192R (rs662)... showed no associations with exceptional longevity.' The original 'medium' confidence was based on the word 'controversial' describing the prior literature, but the replication outcome itself is clear-cut. Upgraded to high.

description: APOE e4 isoform is depleted and e2 isoform is enriched in centenarians compared to controls, showing a consistent genetic association with human longevity
original_authors: Schächter, François; Faure-Delanef, Laurence; Guénot, Frédérique; Rouger, Hervé; Froguel, Philippe; Lesueur-Ginot, Laurence; Cohen, Daniel
original_title: Genetic associations with human longevity at the APOE and ACE loci
replication_authors: Valeria Novelli; Chiara Viviani Anselmi; Roberta Roncarati; Guia Guffanti; Alberto Malovini; Giulio Piluso; Annibale Alessandro Puca
replication_title: Lack of replication of genetic associations with human longevity
explanation: The authors used APOE as a positive control and found: 'The analysis of APOE e2 (TT haplotype) and e4 (CC haplotype) isoforms showed, as expected, that isoform e2 is enriched and isoform e4 is depleted in centenarians compared to controls,' with p=1.05e-05 and p=0.0003 in two independent groups.

description: Mid- to upper-level managers exhibit a Personal-Competence managerial value orientation (MVO) that remains stable across generations, with the majority prioritizing competence values over moral values
original_authors: James Weber
original_title: Managerial value orientations: A typology and assessment
original_journal: International Journal of Value Based Management
replication_authors: James Weber
replication_title: Identifying and Assessing Managerial Value Orientations: A Cross-Generational Replication Study of Key Organizational Decision-Makers’ Values
explanation: The paper explicitly states: 'the primary focus of this research is to explore if the MVO found by Weber (1990) can be replicated in today's business environment.' The replication failed: χ²=199.845 (df=3, p<0.0001) showed significant differences between the 1990 and early 2010s distributions, with the competence MVO declining from 75.3% to 48.8%. The authors conclude: 'Contrary to Oliver (1999) and Posner (2010), MVO have changed over time.'

description: Therapist, team, and country-wide (wave) experience predict therapist adherence in Multisystemic Therapy, and therapist adherence mediates the associations between experience variables and post-treatment outcomes for adolescents with antisocial behavior
original_authors: Cecilia Andrée Löfholm; Kyle Eichas; Knut Sundell
original_title: The Swedish implementation of multisystemic therapy for adolescents: does treatment experience predict treatment adherence?
original_journal: Journal of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology
replication_authors: Aurelie M. C. Lange; Rachel E. A. van der Rijken; Jan J. V. Busschbach; Marc J. M. H. Delsing; Ron H. J. Scholte
replication_title: It’s not just the Therapist: Therapist and Country-Wide Experience Predict Therapist Adherence and Adolescent Outcome
explanation: The authors explicitly replicate the mediation model of Löfholm et al. (2014) in a Dutch sample. The Discussion states: 'The current study replicated the mediation model of Löfholm and colleagues (2014)' but notes key differences: 'Contrary to the study by Löfholm and colleagues (2014), we found therapist experience instead of team experience to predict therapist adherence and treatment outcome.' Country-wide experience was confirmed, but team experience findings were opposite to the original, making the overall result a partial/inconclusive replication.

description: Gender and age of speakers affect speech rate, with older speakers having slower speech rates and male speakers having faster speech rates than female speakers
original_authors: Uriel Cohen Priva; Lee Edelist; Emily Gleason
original_title: Converging to the baseline: Corpus evidence for convergence in speech rate to interlocutor's baseline
original_journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
replication_authors: Simone Fuscone; Benoit Favre; Laurent Prévot
replication_title: Reproducibility in speech rate convergence experiments
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'The results of our reproduction of the study of Cohen Priva et al. (2017) confirmed that the gender and age of speakers affect speech rate production (Study 1), as stated in the original work.' Both age and gender effects were confirmed with similar effect sizes and significance levels.

description: Speakers converge their speech rate toward their interlocutor's baseline speech rate, with both speaker baseline and interlocutor baseline affecting speech rate, and gender combination of speakers also affecting convergence
original_authors: Uriel Cohen Priva; Lee Edelist; Emily Gleason
original_title: Converging to the baseline: Corpus evidence for convergence in speech rate to interlocutor's baseline
original_journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
replication_authors: Simone Fuscone; Benoit Favre; Laurent Prévot
replication_title: Reproducibility in speech rate convergence experiments
explanation: The authors confirmed that both speaker baseline and interlocutor baseline significantly affect speech rate (supporting convergence), but stated: 'contrary to the results of Cohen Priva et al., the gender combination of the speakers and interlocutors was not found to be significant in affecting speech rate.' The main convergence finding was replicated, but a secondary finding about gender interaction was not.

description: Framing climate change responsibility in collective rather than personal terms leads to greater donations to environmental organizations and higher self-reported willingness to reduce emissions
original_authors: Nick Obradovich; Scott M. Guenther
original_title: Collective responsibility amplifies mitigation behaviors
replication_authors: Joseph P. Lavallee; Bruno Di Giusto; Tai-Yi Yu
replication_title: Collective responsibility framing also leads to mitigation behavior in East Asia: a replication study in Taiwan
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a 'partial replication': 'Our study provides a partial replication with a different demographic group and in a different cultural setting.' In the pooled analysis, both collective and personal framing increased donations over control (unlike the original where collective > personal), while the behavioral change finding partially matched the original (personal condition lower than collective/control).

description: Experimentally modulating cognitive immunization (promoting vs. inhibiting it) in a subclinical student sample leads to significant differences in the adjustment of negative performance expectations following unexpectedly positive performance feedback
original_authors: Tobias Kube; Winfried Rief; Mario Gollwitzer; Thomas Gärtner; Julia Anna Glombiewski
original_title: Why dysfunctional expectations in depression persist - results from two experimental studies investigating cognitive immunization
replication_authors: Mimi Houben; Winfried Rief; Thomas Gärtner; Tobias Kube
replication_title: Modulating the Value of Positive Feedback Does Not Influence Expectation Change in Major depression – What Can be Learned from a Failed Replication?
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'the present study failed to replicate that the modulation of cognitive immunization leads to differences in expectation update in depression (Kube et al., 2019b)'. The Time × Condition interaction was non-significant (F(3,135) = 0.57, p = .637, η²p = 0.004), indicating no group differences in expectation updating.

original_authors: Timothy M. Frayling; Nicholas J. Timpson; Michael N. Weedon; Eleftheria Zeggini; Rachel M. Freathy; Cecilia M. Lindgren; John R. B. Perry; Katherine S. Elliott; Hana Lango; Nigel W.
