BC-coalitions formed 67% of the time and A was included in only 19% of coalitions, χ²(2, N=52)=31.89, p<.001, w=0.78.

description: In a three-person coalition game with unequal resources (weighted majority game), the strongest bargainer (Player A with highest weight) is disproportionately excluded from coalitions, with weak players forming coalitions against the strong one (the Strength-is-Weakness effect)
original_authors: W. Edgar Vinacke; Abe Arkoff
original_title: An experimental study of coalitions in the triad
replication_authors: Joeri Wissink; Ilja van Beest; Tila Pronk; Niels van de Ven
replication_title: Strength Is Still a Weakness in Coalition Formation: Replicating and Understanding the Strength-Is-Weakness Effect
explanation: Study 2 replicated the Strength-is-Weakness effect on Amazon Mechanical Turk (online, non-student sample). The authors state: 'Study 2 again replicated the Strength-is-Weakness effect; the BC-coalition was formed substantially more often than the AB- and AC-coalitions.' BC-coalitions formed 65% of the time, A included in only 35% of coalitions, χ²(2, N=80)=40.90, p<.001, w=0.72.

description: In a three-person coalition game with unequal resources (weighted majority game), the strongest bargainer (Player A with highest weight) is disproportionately excluded from coalitions, with weak players forming coalitions against the strong one (the Strength-is-Weakness effect)
original_authors: W. Edgar Vinacke; Abe Arkoff
original_title: An experimental study of coalitions in the triad
replication_authors: Joeri Wissink; Ilja van Beest; Tila Pronk; Niels van de Ven
replication_title: Strength Is Still a Weakness in Coalition Formation: Replicating and Understanding the Strength-Is-Weakness Effect
explanation: Study 3 tested the Strength-is-Weakness effect in a hypothetical political setting (4(322) game) on Prolific. The authors state in the Discussion: 'In Study 3, we obtained additional evidence for the existence of the Strength-is-Weakness effect and the role of application and expectation of the equity norm in a 4(322) political setting.' Weak bargainers made more first offers to each other (n=97) than to the strong bargainer (n=63), χ²(1, N=160)=7.23, p=.01, w=0.21.

description: Exposure to deterministic sentences (reducing free will belief) causes participants to be less willing to help others compared to those who read free will sentences (Study 1 of Baumeister et al., 2009)
original_authors: Baumeister RF; Masicampo EJ; DeWall CN
original_title: Prosocial benefits of feeling free: Disbelief in free will increases aggression and reduces helpfulness
replication_authors: Oliver Genschow
replication_title: It Is Belief in Dualism, and Not Free Will, That Best Predicts Helping: A Conceptual Replication and Extension of Baumeister et al. (2009)
explanation: The authors conducted five high-powered conceptual replications and extensions of Baumeister et al.'s Studies 1 and 2. The Summary states: 'The present study replicated Baumeister et al.'s (2009) finding by demonstrating that belief in free will correlates with helping.' The meta-analysis across all 5 studies found a significant correlation between belief in free will and helping (r = .14, p = .031), supporting the original finding, though it also showed belief in dualism was an even stronger predictor.

description: Belief in free will (measured correlatively) predicts participants' intended helping behavior (hours willing to help) even when controlling for mood (Study 2 of Baumeister et al., 2009)
original_authors: Baumeister RF; Masicampo EJ; DeWall CN
original_title: Prosocial benefits of feeling free: Disbelief in free will increases aggression and reduces helpfulness
replication_authors: Oliver Genschow
replication_title: It Is Belief in Dualism, and Not Free Will, That Best Predicts Helping: A Conceptual Replication and Extension of Baumeister et al. (2009)
explanation: The authors explicitly replicated the correlational approach of Baumeister et al.'s Study 2 across multiple studies, using the same Katie Banks scenario in Study 3. The General Discussion states: 'the meta-analysis supports Baumeister et al.'s findings as belief in free will correlated with helping behavior.' The meta-analytic r = .14 (p = .031) confirms the original correlation, though belief in dualism emerged as the stronger predictor.

description: US American children prioritize humans over animals (dogs and pigs) to a lesser extent than US American adults do in tragic trade-off moral dilemmas
original_authors: Matti Wilks; Lucius Caviola; Guy Kahane; Paul Bloom
original_title: Children prioritize humans over animals less than adults do
replication_authors: Mariola Paruzel-Czachura; Maximilian Maier; Roksana Warmuz; Matti Wilks; Lucius Caviola
replication_title: Children Value Animals More Than Adults Do: A Conceptual Replication and Extension
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'We replicated the main effect, showing that children (Study 1a) prioritize humans over animals less than adults (Study 1b).' This was confirmed by a Replication Bayes Factor analysis yielding BF10 = 1.39 × 10^18, described as 'overwhelming evidence for a successful replication.'

description: Conceptual abstraction moderates whether past moral or immoral behavior leads to consistency or compensatory behavior: recalling moral/immoral behavior from the distant (recent) past leads to consistent (compensatory) prosocial behavior
original_authors: Paul Conway; Johanna Peetz
original_title: When does feeling moral actually make you a better person? Conceptual abstraction moderates whether past moral deeds motivate consistency or compensatory behavior
replication_authors: Jareef Martuza; Olivia Kim
replication_title: Does Conceptual Abstraction Moderate Whether Past Moral Deeds Motivate Consistency or Compensatory Behavior? A Registered Replication and Extension of Conway and Peetz (2012)
explanation: The authors explicitly state that the hypothesized interaction was not replicated: 'the Event Valence X Event Distance interaction effect on WTV was not significant, F(1, 3335) = .176, p = .675' and 'the results did not support conceptual abstraction being a moderator.' The Discussion confirms: 'Our study...tested the hypothesis proposed by Conway and Peetz (2012)...The results did not support conceptual abstraction being a moderator.'

description: Masculine and feminine items in the BSRI are rated by both male and female judges as significantly more desirable in the predicted sex (masculine items more desirable in males, feminine items more desirable in females), enabling sex-typed item selection for the inventory
original_authors: Sandra L. Bem
original_title: The measurement of psychological androgyny
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_authors: Allen L. Edwards; Clark D. Ashworth
replication_title: A Replication Study of Item Selection for the Bem Sex Role Inventory
explanation: In Study 1 (fall 1975), only 1 of 20 masculine items ('masculine') and 1 of 20 feminine items ('feminine') met Bem's criterion of being rated significantly more desirable in the predicted sex by both male and female judges. The authors conclude this is 'in considerable disagreement with the earlier findings of Bem.'

description: Masculine and feminine items in the BSRI are rated by both male and female judges as significantly more desirable in the predicted sex (masculine items more desirable in males, feminine items more desirable in females), enabling sex-typed item selection for the inventory
original_authors: Sandra L. Bem
original_title: The measurement of psychological androgyny
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_authors: Allen L. Edwards; Clark D. Ashworth
replication_title: A Replication Study of Item Selection for the Bem Sex Role Inventory
explanation: In Study 2 (fall 1976), again only 'masculine' and 'feminine' met Bem's criterion. The authors state: 'Again in this second attempt to replicate Bem's results, the only item rated by both males and females as significantly more desirable in a male than in a female was masculine, and the only item rated by both males and females as significantly more desirable in a female was feminine.'

description: Confirmatory factor analysis of the LSP-16 reveals poor psychometric properties (high residual error, low factor loadings) that do not support its proposed four-factor structure
original_authors: Graham D. Bodie; Debra L. Worthington
original_title: Revisiting the Listening Styles Profile (LSP-16): A confirmatory factor analytic approach to scale validation and reliability estimation
replication_authors: Brett Williams; Ted Brown; Malcolm Boyle
replication_title: Psychometric Properties of the Listening Styles Profile (LSP-16)
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'The CFA results in our study mirror those obtained by Bodie and Worthington (2010) suggesting that the LSP-16 be revised.' The study is explicitly described as 'a replication study' in its title, testing the same CFA methodology in a cross-cultural (Australian) context, and successfully reproduced the finding that the LSP-16 has poor psychometric properties.

description: The COMT Val/Val genotype is associated with a good methylphenidate treatment response in terms of hyperactive-impulsive (but not inattentive) symptoms in children with ADHD
original_authors: Eva Kereszturi; Zsanett Tarnok; Emese Bognar; Krisztina Lakatos; Luca Farkas; Julia Gadoros; Maria Sasvari‐Szekely; Zsofia Nemoda
original_title: Catechol-O-methyltransferase Val-158Met polymorphism is associated with methylphenidate response in ADHD children
original_journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part B: Neuropsychiatric Genetics
replication_authors: Subin Park; Jae-Won Kim; Bung-Nyun Kim; Min-Sup Shin; Hee-Jeong Yoo; Soo-Churl Cho
replication_title: Catechol-O-methyltransferase Val 158 -Met polymorphism and a response of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms to methylphenidate: A replication study from South Korea
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'Consistent with a previous study (Kereszturi et al., 2008), we found a significant association between the COMT (Val158-Met) polymorphism genotype and treatment response to MPH, such that ADHD subjects with the Val/Val genotype showed a better treatment response in terms of hyperactive-impulsive, but not inattentive symptoms.' The replication succeeded in a Korean sample with OR=2.61 (p=0.044).

description: Ketamine has rapid-onset anxiolytic effects in patients with treatment-resistant generalized anxiety disorder and social anxiety disorder, with a dose-response relationship in an open-label design
original_authors: Paul Glue; Natalie J. Medlicott; Sarah Harland; Shona Neehoff; Bridie Anderson-Fahey; Martin Le Nedelec; Andrew Gray; Neil McNaughton
original_title: Ketamine's dose-related effects on anxiety symptoms in patients with treatment refractory anxiety disorders
replication_authors: Paul Glue; Shona Neehoff; Amandine Sabadel; Lucy Broughton; Martin Le Nedelec; Shabah Shadli; Neil McNaughton; Natalie J. Medlicott
replication_title: Effects of ketamine in patients with treatment-refractory generalized anxiety and social anxiety disorders: Exploratory double-blind psychoactive-controlled replication study
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'This study is a replication of our initial report of ketamine's anxiolytic effects (Glue et al., 2017), but using a more robust design (double blind, psychoactive controlled).' Significant dose-related anxiolytic effects were replicated (HAM-A vs dose: p < 0.001), confirming the original finding.

description: The three most commonly reported benefits of microdosing psychedelics (LSD or psilocybin) are improved mood, improved focus, and increased creativity; the three most commonly reported challenges are concerns about illegality, physiological discomfort, and impaired focus
original_authors: Thomas Anderson; Rotem Petranker; Adam Christopher; Daniel Rosenbaum; Cory Weissman; Le-Anh Dinh-Williams; Katrina Hui; Emma Hapke
original_title: Psychedelic microdosing benefits and challenges: An empirical codebook
replication_authors: Rotem Petranker; Thomas Anderson; Larissa J. Maier; Monica J. Barratt; Jason A. Ferris; Adam R. Winstock
replication_title: Microdosing psychedelics: Subjective benefits and challenges, substance testing behavior, and the relevance of intention
explanation: The authors explicitly describe this as a 'partial replication': improved mood and creativity replicated as top benefits, but improved focus was not in the top three; for challenges, 'None' was the most commonly reported, not illegality, which the authors acknowledge as counter to their hypothesis. The Discussion notes: 'Similar but non-identical findings are not surprising given that the methodologies used in the two studies were quite different.'

description: Clinicians intuitively prescribe lower risperidone doses to CYP2D6 poor metabolizer patients with first-episode psychosis, without knowledge of the patient's genotype
original_authors: Mas S.; Gassò P.; Alvarez S.; Parellada E.; Bernardo M.; Lafuente A.
original_title: Intuitive pharmacogenetics: spontaneous risperidone dosage is related to CYP2D6, CYP3A4 and ABCB1 genotypes
replication_authors: Emma Y. De Brabander; Thérèse van Amelsvoort; Roos van Westrhenen
replication_title: Unidentified CYP2D6 genotype does not affect pharmacological treatment for patients with first episode psychosis
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'our hypothesis that medication dose was unintentionally already adapted to the patients' CYP2D6 phenotype was rejected' and 'our results contrast with the original studies by Mas et al. (2012, 2017), as we could not reproduce similar findings entirely.' No significant correlation between CYP2D6 phenotype and chlorpromazine-equivalent dose was found (complete sample: p=0.3, risperidone-only: p=0.34).

description: Clinicians intuitively adjust risperidone dosage according to CYP2D6 phenotype in first-episode psychosis patients receiving medication for less than one year, with reduced metabolizer status associated with lower prescribed doses

original_title: Intuitive pharmacogenetic dosing of risperidone according to CYP2D6 phenotype extrapolated from genotype in a cohort of first episode psychosis patients

replication_title: Unidentified CYP2D6 genotype does not affect pharmacological treatment for patients with first episode psychosis
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'our hypothesis that medication dose was unintentionally already adapted to the patients' CYP2D6 phenotype was rejected' and 'our results contrast with the original studies by Mas et al. (2012, 2017), as we could not reproduce similar findings entirely.' No significant correlation between CYP2D6 phenotype and risperidone-equivalent dose was found (risperidone-only: p=0.34).

description: Same-day test-retest [11C]ABP688 PET studies in healthy male humans show significant within-subject increases in mGluR5 binding (VT and BPND) between the first and second same-day scans
original_authors: DeLorenzo C.; Kumar JS; Mann JJ; Parsey RV
original_title: In vivo variation in metabotropic glutamate receptor subtype 5 binding using positron emission tomography and [11C]ABP688
original_journal: Journal of Cerebral Blood Flow & Metabolism

replication_title: In vivo variation in same-day estimates of metabotropic glutamate receptor subtype 5 binding using [<sup>11</sup>C]ABP688 and [<sup>18</sup>F]FPEB
replication_journal: Journal of Cerebral Blood Flow & Metabolism
explanation: The authors explicitly frame this as a replication study: 'the goals of the current study were to determine whether the findings in males were replicable.' Results confirmed the original finding, with 7 of 11 subjects showing increased binding (p<0.01), consistent with the original study's 7 of 8 subjects showing increases. The conclusion states: 'Study results show increases in [11C]ABP688 and [18F]FPEB binding for most subjects between same-day test-retest studies in both sexes. The results are consistent with previous same-day test-retest studies for [11C]ABP688.'

description: Higher media multitasking in adolescents is related to more self-reported executive functioning difficulties but not to poorer performance on computerized executive functioning tasks (working memory, inhibition, task-shifting)
original_authors: Susanne E. Baumgartner; Wouter D. Weeda; Lisa L. van der Heijden; Mariëtte Huizinga
original_title: The relationship between media multitasking and executive function in early adolescents
replication_authors: Doris Antonia Rogobete; Thea Ionescu; Mircea Miclea
replication_title: The Relationship Between Media Multitasking Behavior and Executive Function in Adolescence: A Replication Study
explanation: The authors state results were 'partially replicated': some findings were confirmed (MM with media predicts self-reported WM and inhibition difficulties; no relation between MM and computerized task performance in continuous analyses; extreme group differences in self-reported EF), while others were not (MM did not predict self-reported shifting difficulties; MMI-NM did not predict any EF difficulties; HMMs responded faster than LMMs on computerized tasks, contrasting with the original).

description: Students who receive an objective multiple-choice examination with a forward-sequential item order (matching the order material was presented in lectures) perform better than those who receive the same exam with a randomized question order
original_authors: Pettit, Kathy L.; Baker, Kenneth G.; Davis, Laura D.
original_title: Unconscious biasing of student examination scores: a case of sequential versus random information retrieval
replication_authors: Rowland C. Chidomere
replication_title: Test Item Arrangement and Student Performance in Principles of Marketing Examination: A Replication Study
explanation: The paper explicitly states it replicates Pettit et al. (1986) and concludes: 'The finding of no significant difference between the various test scores in test forms analyzed in the present study conflicts with the findings of Pettit et al. (1986).' None of the three ANOVAs (Exams I, III, and II vs. IV) showed a statistically significant difference between forward-sequential and randomized item order.

description: Completing a face matching task in a pair leads to improved accuracy during pairing and a sustained training benefit for the lower performer in the pair compared to the higher performer
original_authors: Dowsett AJ; Burton AM
original_title: Unfamiliar face matching: Pairs out-perform individuals and provide a route to training
replication_authors: Kay L. Ritchie; Tessa R. Flack; Elizabeth A. Fuller; Charlotte Cartledge; Robin S. S. Kramer
replication_title: The pairs training effect in unfamiliar face matching
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'This experiment replicated the pairs effect described by Dowsett and Burton (2015).' Both Experiments 1 and 2 show significant accuracy improvements from T1 to T2 (paired session) and lasting benefit at T3, particularly for low performers, fully replicating the core pairs training effect.

description: Completing a face matching task in a pair leads to improved accuracy during pairing and a sustained training benefit for the lower performer in the pair compared to the higher performer
original_authors: Dowsett AJ; Burton AM
original_title: Unfamiliar face matching: Pairs out-perform individuals and provide a route to training
replication_authors: Kay L. Ritchie; Tessa R. Flack; Elizabeth A. Fuller; Charlotte Cartledge; Robin S. S. Kramer
replication_title: The pairs training effect in unfamiliar face matching
explanation: The authors state: 'These results replicated both Dowsett and Burton (2015) and the pairs training effect reported in Experiment 1.' Low performers showed significant accuracy improvement from T1 to T3 (d = 1.48, p < .001), confirming the training effect in a second independent sample.

description: High perceptual load (target array with confusable non-target letters) reduces or abolishes congruence effects from a distractor letter compared to low perceptual load
original_authors: Nilli Lavie; Sally Cox
original_title: On the efficiency of visual selective attention: Efficient visual search leads to inefficient distractor rejection
replication_authors: Robert J. Snowden; Nicola S. Gray
replication_title: Reduction in distraction due to perceptual load: A failure to replicate
explanation: Across six experiments the authors found strong distraction and congruence effects at both low and high perceptual load with no significant interaction, directly contradicting the classic perceptual load prediction. They conclude: 'we have failed to replicate, over a wide range of conditions, the standard finding that distraction effects are reduced/eliminated under conditions of high perceptual load.'

description: A neutral distractor produces a distraction effect (slower RTs vs. no distractor) at low perceptual load, but this effect is reduced or abolished at high perceptual load
original_authors: Sophie Forster; Nilli Lavie
original_title: Failures to ignore entirely irrelevant distractors: The role of load
replication_authors: Robert J. Snowden; Nicola S. Gray
replication_title: Reduction in distraction due to perceptual load: A failure to replicate
explanation: The paper explicitly cites Forster and Lavie (2008) as the source for the distraction effect reduced at high load, and across six experiments finds that distraction effects (neutral distractor vs. no distractor) were present at both low and high perceptual load with no significant difference, failing to replicate this key result. The load × distractor interaction was non-significant across all experiments (e.g., Experiment 1: F(1.8, 63.7) = 0.05, p = .98).

description: Small ensemble participation frequency is a significant positive predictor of empathy skill among college music performance students
original_authors: Eun Cho
original_title: The relationship between small music ensemble experience and empathy skill: A survey study
replication_authors: Eun Cho; Jeoung Yeoun Han
replication_title: Small music ensemble and empathy: A replication study in a South Korean music student sample
explanation: The authors explicitly state that results 'partially replicated the initial study': some findings were consistent (popular music majors scoring higher in empathy than classical music majors), while others failed to replicate (age at commencement of music training no longer significant; only informal SE, not both formal and informal SE, predicted empathy). The authors conclude 'this study partially replicated the initial study.'

description: A school-based assessment and individualized support intervention (Skolfam model) improves cognitive performance, spelling, word comprehension, and reading speed for foster children over a two-year follow-up
original_authors: Eva Tideman; Bo Vinnerljung; Kristin Hintze; Anna Aldenius Isaksson
original_title: Improving foster children's school achievements: promising results from a Swedish intensive study
replication_authors: Rikard Tordön; Bo Vinnerljung; Ulla Axelsson
replication_title: Improving foster children’s school performance: a replication of the Helsingborg study
explanation: The authors explicitly confirm success: 'This study confirms the conclusions from the Helsingborg trial (Tideman, et al., 2011). Poor results in school performance for children in foster care can be improved with an intervention based on an educational and psychological assessment, followed by an individual, coached progress plan.' Results on literacy and numeracy were on par with or better than the Helsingborg study.

description: Increased cortical thickness in the somatosensory cortex (SSC/SMC) in patients with migraine compared to healthy controls

replication_authors: Ritobrato Datta; John A. Detre; Geoffrey K. Aguirre; Brett Cucchiara
replication_title: Absence of changes in cortical thickness in patients with migraine
explanation: The authors explicitly aimed to 'independently replicate the reported findings of increased cortical thickness in the SSC' using the same surface-based morphometry method. They found 'no significant differences in mean thickness of the SMC or PCS between the MWA, MwoA, and control groups' and concluded that 'no differences in cortical thickness between patients with migraine and controls could be identified.'

description: Increased gray matter thickness in visual motion processing areas (V3A and MT+) in patients with migraine compared to healthy controls

original_title: Anatomical alterations of the visual motion processing network in migraine with and without aura
replication_authors: Ritobrato Datta; John A. Detre; Geoffrey K. Aguirre; Brett Cucchiara
replication_title: Absence of changes in cortical thickness in patients with migraine
explanation: The authors explicitly aimed to replicate the finding of increased cortical thickness in visual motion processing areas (V3A and MT+) reported by Granziera et al. (9). They found 'no difference in cortical thickness across groups' for both V3A and MT+ regions, and concluded that 'no differences in cortical thickness between patients with migraine and controls could be identified.'

explanation: The authors found nominal associations for two of three SNPs from Chasman et al. (2011) — rs2651899 (PRDM16, p=0.0056) and rs10166942 (TRPM8, p=0.0442) — but neither survived multiple testing corrections. The authors conclude 'our study provides suggestive replication' of four GWAS findings, framing the results as partial and uncertain.

explanation: The authors tested nine SNPs from Anttila et al. (2013) and found that 'the evaluation of the remaining nine SNPs, selected from the meta-analysis study performed by Anttila et al. (4), failed to replicate any of the associations in our MA sample' in the main analysis, though two SNPs (rs12134493 near TSPAN2 and rs10504861 near MMP16) showed nominal associations in the 'Both MA and MO' subgroup. The authors describe results as 'suggestive replication' but note findings do not attain statistical significance.

replication_journal: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
explanation: The authors explicitly state their purpose was to 'Replicate prior findings of a bifactor structure of concussion symptoms' from their previous smaller study. They confirm the bifactor model fit well in the larger, more diverse CARE Consortium sample, finding a 7-factor bifactor model (extending the original 5-factor model), and state 'The findings expand upon evidence that the structure of concussion symptoms is best delineated using a bifactor modeling approach.'

description: The 1989 Quebec prevalence survey found that 54% of adults had gambled in the past year and that the lifetime rate of pathological gambling was 1.2%, establishing a baseline prevalence estimate for pathological gambling in Quebec
original_authors: Robert Ladouceur
original_title: Prevalence estimates of pathological gambling in Quebec
replication_authors: Robert Ladouceur; Christian Jacques; Francine Ferland; Isabelle Giroux
replication_title: Prevalence of Problem Gambling: A Replication Study 7 Years Later
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'the prevalence study conducted in 1989 was replicated in 1996' using the same South Oaks Gambling Screen methodology. The replication confirmed the link between gambling availability and problem gambling prevalence, finding significant increases in gambling participation (54% to 63%) and pathological gambling rates (1.2% to 2.1%), consistent with the original study's framing.

description: Vocabulary-Matching (VM) outperforms Statement Verification for Science (SV-S) as a curriculum-based measurement screening tool for middle school science, with VM showing stronger alternate form reliability, criterion validity, and predictive utility
original_authors: Jeremy W. Ford; Sarah J. Conoyer; Erica S. Lembke; R. Alex Smith; John L. Hosp
original_title: A comparison of two content area curriculum-based measurement tools
replication_authors: Sarah J. Conoyer; Jeremy W. Ford; R. Alex Smith; Erica N. Mason; Erica S. Lembke; John L. Hosp
replication_title: Examining Curriculum-Based Measurement Screening Tools in Middle School Science: A Scaled Replication Study
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'we sought to replicate Ford et al. (2018) with a larger sample size, adjusted development and administration procedures for SV-S, and a different state standardized science assessment' and label it a 'conceptual replication.' The Discussion confirms: 'This pattern of the VM measure outperforming the SV-S measure is similar to results found in the Ford et al. (2018) study,' indicating the core finding was replicated, though SV-S produced stronger coefficients with the larger sample.

description: Uses-and-gratifications statements about newspapers reduce to three distinct factor groupings (surveillance, diversion, and interaction), which predict weekday and Sunday newspaper readership behaviors among different reader types
original_authors: Towers, Wayne M.
original_title: Weekday and Sunday readership seen through uses and gratifications
replication_authors: Wayne M. Towers
replication_title: Replication of a Study on Uses and Gratifications for Weekday and Sunday Readers
explanation: The replication found only two factors (Information and Entertainment) instead of the original three (surveillance, diversion, interaction), failing Hypothesis 1. However, the discriminant analysis provided limited support for some readership hypotheses (e.g., subscribers' orientation toward immediate news). The authors conclude: 'The research affirmed the consistency of some variables and concepts, but it also demonstrated the inconsistency of others.'

description: The 18-item Index of Sojourner Social Support (ISSS) measures two distinct latent factors — socioemotional support (items 1-9) and instrumental support (items 10-18) — among sojourners living outside their country of origin
original_authors: Andy S. J. Ong; Colleen Ward
original_title: The construction and validation of a social support measure for sojourners: The Index of Sojourner Social Support (ISSS) Scale
replication_authors: Paul A. Gilbert; Scott D. Rhodes
replication_title: Psychometric Performance of a Novel Measure of Social Support Among Spanish-Speaking Immigrant Latino Gay Men
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'We failed to replicate the two-factor structure, indicating that a distinction between social-emotional and instrumental support is not supported by our data.' The confirmatory factor analysis found an unacceptably high correlation between the two latent factors (r = .968), indicating they were not distinct constructs in this sample.

description: A path model of student progress in distance education, using the DESP inventory, showing that social and academic integration act as intervening variables between background characteristics and outcome measures (GPA and course completion)
original_authors: Kember, David; Murphy, David; Siaw, Irene; Yuen, K.S.
original_title: Towards a causal model of student progress in distance education
replication_authors: David Kember; Tammy Lai; David Mlurphy; Irene Siaw; K.S. Yuen
replication_title: Student Progress In Distance Education Courses: A Replication Study
explanation: The authors explicitly confirm replication success in the Discussion: 'There is sufficient similarity between the two path models to confirm the substantive findings of the initial study.' A similar path model was found with a comparable R² for the dropout ratio outcome (0.78 vs. 0.80), and the factor structure showed little deviation from the original study.

description: Autistic individuals show a body burden of neurotoxicants (>90%) and 100% demonstrate impaired liver detoxication processes, supporting a neurotoxic etiology of autism spectrum disorders
