replication_title: Alcohol-Related Impairments in Male Alcoholics and the Psychiatric Symptoms of Their Spouses: An Attempt to Replicate
replication_journal: The American Journal of Drug and Alcohol Abuse
explanation: Sample 2 (Jacob, N=27) found only borderline significant (p < .10) correlations between husband's social impairment and wife's symptoms on a few MMPI scales and BDI. Authors concluded 'Steinglass' major finding is again replicated, although somewhat weakly.'

description: Occasional faculty developers at a research-rich US medical school describe how their professional identities change over time, emerging in four forms: merged, compartmentalized, hierarchical, and parallel identities
original_authors: O'Sullivan, Patricia S.; Irby, David M.
original_title: Identity formation of occasional faculty developers in medical education: A qualitative study
replication_authors: Patricia S. O’Sullivan; Charles Mkony; Jessica Beard; David M. Irby
replication_title: Identity formation and motivation of new faculty developers: A replication study in a resource constrained university
explanation: The authors explicitly designed this study to replicate the UCSF identity findings and conclude in the Discussion: 'we were able largely to replicate the findings concerning identity development as a faculty developer.' Results were 'remarkably similar' with three of the four identity types (merged, compartmentalized, hierarchical) found, though the parallel identity was absent in the MUHAS sample.

description: Occasional faculty developers at a research-rich US medical school are motivated by five themes: satisfaction, mastery, relatedness, duty, and purpose
original_authors: O'Sullivan, Patricia S.; Irby, David M.
original_title: Why does a faculty member teach in faculty development workshops?
replication_authors: Patricia S. O’Sullivan; Charles Mkony; Jessica Beard; David M. Irby
replication_title: Identity formation and motivation of new faculty developers: A replication study in a resource constrained university
explanation: The authors explicitly designed this study to replicate the UCSF motivation findings and conclude they 'were able largely to replicate the findings concerning...motivation to be a faculty developer.' All five motivational themes (mastery, purpose, duty, satisfaction, relatedness) found at UCSF were also found at MUHAS: 'All five themes about what motivated participants to be a faculty developer that were found at UCSF also were found at MUHAS.'

description: The SNP rs2352028 in GPC5 is associated with increased risk of lung cancer in never-smokers (p = 5.94×10⁻⁶, OR = 1.46)
original_authors: Li Y.; Sheu CC; Ye Y.; de Andrade M.; Wang L.; Chang SC; Aubry MC; Aakre JA; Allen MS; Chen F.; Cunningham JM; Deschamps C.; Jiang R.; Lin J.; Marks RS; Pankratz VS; Su L.; Li Y.; Sun Z.; Tang H.; Vasmatzis G.; Harris CC; Spitz MR; Jen J.; Wang R.; Zhang ZF; Christiani DC; Wu X.; Yang P.
original_title: Genetic variants and risk of lung cancer in never smokers: a genome-wide association study
replication_authors: Yonglan Zheng; Mengyuan Kan; Lan Yu; Xiaomin Niu; Daizhan Zhou; Lin He; Shun Lu; Yun Liu
replication_title: GPC5rs2352028 Polymorphism and Risk of Lung Cancer in Han Chinese
explanation: The authors explicitly state: 'We failed to replicate the association of rs2352028 in GPC5 with lung cancer in never-smokers found by Li and colleagues.' No statistically significant associations were found between rs2352028 and lung cancer or adenocarcinoma in never-smokers (all p > .05) in the Han Chinese cohort.

description: Genetic variants at the 10p12.31-12.2 locus (including rs4266962, rs4748793, rs7901152, rs7075634, rs7088318, rs11013046) are associated with susceptibility to childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia in ethnically diverse populations
original_authors: Xu H.; Yang W.; Perez-Andreu V.; Devidas M.; Fan Y.; Cheng C.; Pei D.; Scheet P.; Burchard EG; Eng C.; Huntsman S.; Torgerson DG; Dean M.; Winick NJ; Martin PL; Camitta BM; Bowman WP; Willman CL; Carroll WL; Mullighan CG; Bhojwani D.; Hunger SP; Pui CH; Evans WE; Relling MV; Loh ML; Yang JJ
original_title: Novel susceptibility variants at 10p12.31-12.2 for childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia in ethnically diverse populations
original_journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
replication_authors: Jianping Deng; Yao Xue; Yaping Wang; Jing Chen; Jie Li; Qin Lu; Meilin Wang; Na Tong; Zhengdong Zhang; Yongjun Fang
replication_title: 10p12.31-12.2 variants and risk of childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia in a Chinese population
explanation: The authors confirmed 4 of 6 SNPs (rs7075634, rs7088318, rs7901152, rs11013046 in PIP4K2A) were associated with childhood ALL risk in the Chinese population, but 2 SNPs (rs4266962 and rs4748793) were not significantly associated. The conclusion states 'our replication study confirmed that four novel variants...were associated with susceptibility to pediatric ALL in a Chinese Han population,' but notably failed to replicate 2 of the original 6 variants.

description: Relapse determinants among alcoholics can be classified into intrapersonal and interpersonal situational categories, with intrapersonal determinants (especially negative emotional states) being the most common precipitants of relapse
original_authors: Marlatt, G.A.; Gordon, F.R.
original_title: Determinants of relapse: Implications for the maintenance of behavior change
replication_authors: Christer Sandahl
replication_title: Determinants of Relapse among Alcoholics: A Cross-Cultural Replication Study
explanation: The authors explicitly state the study replicates Marlatt and Gordon (1980) in a different cultural context (Sweden vs. Seattle). Despite differences in drinking culture (e.g., location of first drink: 56% at home in Stockholm vs. 63% in bars in Seattle), the paper concludes: 'we arrive at a similar picture when it comes to the distribution of relapse determinants according to the model proposed by Marlatt and Gordon,' and that the categories have 'both face and conceptual validity.'

description: An MMPI-derived AMA Scale is capable of identifying individuals likely to drop out of inpatient chemical dependency treatment using a cut-off score of 8 or above
original_authors: Bernard J. Sladen; Gerald J. Mozdzierz
original_title: An MMPI scale to predict premature termination from inpatient alcohol treatment
replication_authors: Harold E. Doweiko
replication_title: The Sladen and Mozdzierz AMA Scale: A Failed Replication Attempt
explanation: The replication failed to find significant predictive validity for the AMA Scale. The chi-square analysis was non-significant (χ²(1, N=65) = 0.70, p = .781), only 52% of cases were correctly classified (near chance), and only 33% of actual dropouts were identified. The authors explicitly state: 'this study failed to uncover evidence that the AMA Scale advanced by Sladen and Mozdzierz (1985) was capable of the identification of individuals who were unlikely to successfully complete inpatient treatment.'

description: Family therapy for drug abusers produces significantly higher abstinence rates than methadone maintenance and individual counseling as a control treatment
original_authors: Stanton, M.D.; Todd, T.C.
original_title: The family therapy of drug abuse and addiction
original_journal: The Family Therapy of Drug Abuse and Addiction
replication_authors: Clemens M. Romijn; Jerome J. Piatt; Gerard M. Schippers
replication_title: Family Therapy for Dutch Drug Abusers: Replication of an American Study
explanation: The paper 'partly confirmed' Stanton and Todd's findings: the Dutch family therapy group showed similar abstinence rates (64% vs. 60% for heroin) to the original study's family therapy group, but failed to show statistically significant superiority over the methadone control group. The authors explain this as due to the Dutch control group performing better than Stanton and Todd's control group, rather than a failure of family therapy itself.

description: SNPs in the SFRS3 (rs7759778, rs1406945) and FKBP4 (rs2968909) genes are associated with corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension (steroid response) in patients treated with glucocorticoids
original_authors: John H. Fingert; Wallace L. Alward; Kai Wang; Thomas Yorio; Abbot F. Clark
original_title: Assessment of SNPs associated with the human glucocorticoid receptor in primary open-angle glaucoma and steroid responders
replication_authors: Barend F. Hogewind; Shazia Micheal; Bjorn Bakker; Carel B. Hoyng; Anneke I. den Hollander
replication_title: Analysis of single nucleotide polymorphisms in theSFRS3andFKBP4genes in corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension
explanation: The authors explicitly state they performed 'an independent replication study' of Fingert et al. (2010). The conclusion is unambiguous: 'This study does not confirm a role for genetic variants in the SFRS3 and FKBP4 genes in the pathogenesis of corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension.' None of the three SNPs showed significant differences in genotype or allele frequencies between responders and non-responders (all p > 0.05).

description: SNPs in the NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) gene are not significantly associated with steroid-induced ocular hypertension in patients treated with corticosteroids
original_authors: John H. Fingert; Wallace L. Alward; Kai Wang; Thomas Yorio; Abbot F. Clark
original_title: Assessment of SNPs associated with the human glucocorticoid receptor in primary open-angle glaucoma and steroid responders
replication_authors: Barend F. Hogewind; Shazia Micheal; Frederieke E. Schoenmaker-Koller; Carel B. Hoyng; Anneke I. den Hollander
replication_title: Analyses of Sequence Variants in theMYOCGene and of Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms in theNR3C1andFKBP5Genes in Corticosteroid-Induced Ocular Hypertension
explanation: Reviewer upgrade to high confidence. The abstract explicitly calls this 'an independent replication study.' The Discussion unambiguously states: 'We also did not detect significant associations between steroid response and 31 tagging SNPs in NR3C1 and FKBP5... This rules out a major role of these genes in steroid-induced ocular hypertension and correlates with the results of previous studies that did not identify significant associations for several polymorphisms in the NR3C1 and FKBP5 genes [refs 15,16].' Both the original (Fingert et al. 2010, null finding for GR SNPs) and this replication (null finding for 21 NR3C1 tagging SNPs in a Dutch IVTA cohort) converge clearly. Result is 'success' because the original null finding is replicated. Classified as 'close extension' because this study uses a different population (Dutch IVTA patients vs. the original's POAG/steroid responder cohort) and a broader set of 21 tagging SNPs, testing generalizability of the null association to a new context. Table 1 confirms all 21 NR3C1 SNPs have p > 0.05 for both allele and genotype frequencies.

description: Glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) polymorphisms are not significantly associated with intraocular pressure response to intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide
original_authors: Gerzenstein SM; Pletcher MT; Cervino AC; Tsinoremas NF; Young B.; Puliafito CA; Fini ME; Schwartz SG
original_title: Glucocorticoid receptor polymorphisms and intraocular pressure response to intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide
replication_authors: Barend F. Hogewind; Shazia Micheal; Frederieke E. Schoenmaker-Koller; Carel B. Hoyng; Anneke I. den Hollander
replication_title: Analyses of Sequence Variants in theMYOCGene and of Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms in theNR3C1andFKBP5Genes in Corticosteroid-Induced Ocular Hypertension
explanation: Reviewer upgrade to high confidence. The abstract explicitly calls this 'an independent replication study.' The Discussion unambiguously states their null findings 'correlate with the results of previous studies that did not identify significant associations for several polymorphisms in the NR3C1 and FKBP5 genes' (citing Gerzenstein et al. 2008 as ref 16). Both Gerzenstein et al. (2008) and this study examined GR polymorphisms in IVTA-treated patients and found no significant association with IOP response. Result is 'success' because the original null finding is replicated. Classified as 'close extension' because this study uses a different population (native Dutch cohort, n=102) and a broader SNP panel (21 NR3C1 tagging SNPs vs. the original's smaller set of candidate polymorphisms), testing whether the null association generalizes. Table 1 confirms all NR3C1 and FKBP5 SNPs are non-significant (all p > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction).

description: Six CCT-associated SNPs (FNDC3B rs4894535, MPDZ-NF1B rs1324183, RXRA-COL5A1 rs1536482, COL5A1 rs7044529, FOXO1 rs2721051, and BANP-ZNF469 rs9938149) identified by GWAS are associated with keratoconus susceptibility in Australians and Americans of European ancestry
original_authors: Lu Y.; Vitart V.; Burdon KP; Khor CC; Bykhovskaya Y.; Mirshahi A.; Hewitt AW; Koehn D.; Hysi PG; Ramdas WD; Zeller T.; Vithana EN; Cornes BK; Tay WT; Tai ES; Cheng CY; Liu J.; Foo JN; Saw SM; Thorleifsson G.; Stefansson K.; Dimasi DP; Mills RA; Mountain J.; Ang W.; Hoehn R.; Verhoeven VJ; Grus F.; Wolfs R.; Castagne R.; Lackner KJ; Springelkamp H.; Yang J.; Jonasson F.; Leung DY; Chen LJ; Tham CC; Rudan I.; Vatavuk Z.; Hayward C.; Gibson J.; Cree AJ; MacLeod A.; Ennis S.; Polasek O.; Campbell H.; Wilson JF; Viswanathan AC; Fleck B.; Li X.; Siscovick D.; Taylor KD; Rotter JI; Yazar S.; Ulmer M.; Li J.; Yaspan BL; Ozel AB; Richards JE; Moroi SE; Haines JL; Kang JH; Pasquale LR; Allingham RR; Ashley-Koch A.; Mitchell P.; Wang JJ; Wright AF; Pennell C.; Spector TD; Young TL; Klaver CC; Martin NG; Montgomery GW; Anderson MG; Aung T.; Willoughby CE; Wiggs JL; Pang CP; Thorsteinsdottir U.; Lotery AJ; Hammond CJ; van Duijn CM; Hauser MA; Rabinowitz YS; Pfeiffer N.; Mackey DA; Craig JE; Macgregor S.; Wong TY
original_title: Genome-wide association analyses identify multiple loci associated with central corneal thickness and keratoconus
replication_authors: Xiao-Dan Hao; Peng Chen; Zhao-Li Chen; Su-Xia Li; Ye Wang
replication_title: Evaluating the Association between Keratoconus and Reported Genetic Loci in a Han Chinese Population
explanation: Of the six SNPs from Lu et al. (2013), only rs1324183 (MPDZ-NF1B) significantly replicated in the Han Chinese population (OR=3.108, p=0.005, surviving Bonferroni correction). The remaining five SNPs showed no significant association, with two (rs2721051, rs9938149) showing negligible MAF. The authors conclude 'we were able to replicate an association of rs1324183 (MPDZ-NF1B) with KC in our cohort' but not the others.

description: Variation in the LOX gene (rs2956540) is associated with increased susceptibility to keratoconus in American family-based and case-control samples
original_authors: Yelena Bykhovskaya; Xiaohui Li; Irina Epifantseva; Talin Haritunians; David Siscovick; Anthony Aldave; Loretta Szczotka-Flynn; Sudha K. Iyengar; Kent D. Taylor; Jerome I. Rotter; Yaron S. Rabinowitz

replication_authors: Xiao-Dan Hao; Peng Chen; Zhao-Li Chen; Su-Xia Li; Ye Wang
replication_title: Evaluating the Association between Keratoconus and Reported Genetic Loci in a Han Chinese Population
explanation: The minor allele G of rs2956540 (LOX) showed a nominally significant reduced risk of KC in the Chinese population (OR=0.664, 95% CI=0.447-0.986, p=0.042 under dominant model), but this was no longer significant after Bonferroni correction. The authors state 'SNP rs2956540 (LOX) may confer a reduced risk of KC with a borderline p value' and call for future replication in a larger sample.

Rabinowitz; Colin Willoughby; Jamie E. Craig
original_title: Association of polymorphisms in the hepatocyte growth factor gene promoter with keratoconus
replication_authors: Xiao-Dan Hao; Peng Chen; Zhao-Li Chen; Su-Xia Li; Ye Wang
replication_title: Evaluating the Association between Keratoconus and Reported Genetic Loci in a Han Chinese Population
explanation: No significant difference was observed between patients and controls for rs3735520 (Near HGF) genotype or allele frequencies (p=0.474). The authors conclude 'these polymorphisms confer no effect on the risk of KC in our Chinese population.'

original_authors: Xiaohui Li; Yelena Bykhovskaya; Talin Haritunians; David Siscovick; Anthony Aldave; Loretta Szczotka-Flynn; Sudha K. Iyengar; Jerome I. Rotter; Kent D. Taylor; Yaron S. Rabinowitz

replication_title: Evaluating the Association between Keratoconus and Reported Genetic Loci in a Han Chinese Population
explanation: rs4954218 had a MAF of zero in both patients and controls in the Han Chinese population, making it impossible to test the association. The allele appears to be absent in this population, consistent with different genetic backgrounds between Chinese and Caucasian populations.

description: SNP rs6050307 in the VSX1 gene is significantly associated with keratoconus in a Han Chinese population
original_authors: Yani Wang; Tianbo Jin; Xuehui Zhang; Wei Wei; Yan Cui; Tingting Geng; Qianping Liu; Jing Gao; Ming Liu; Chao Chen; Changning Zhang; Xiuping Zhu
original_title: Common single nucleotide polymorphisms and keratoconus in the Han Chinese population

replication_title: Evaluating the Association between Keratoconus and Reported Genetic Loci in a Han Chinese Population
explanation: REVIEWER NOTE: rs6050307 (VSX1) had a MAF of zero in both patients (n=210) and controls (n=191) — the variant was completely absent from this Han Chinese sample. The authors group it with the eight non-replicated SNPs, stating 'these polymorphisms confer no effect on the risk of KC in our Chinese population.' Classification as 'failure' is defensible since the original finding (Wang et al. 2013, also in Han Chinese) cannot be confirmed, but confidence remains medium because MAF=0 means the association was literally untestable rather than tested-and-negative — a case could be made for 'inconclusive' on those grounds.

description: A non-quantity-based single item assessing drunkenness ('How often did you typically get drunk?') can accurately detect hazardous alcohol use as identified by AUDIT-C scores, demonstrating concurrent and convergent validity
original_authors: Adam E. Barry; Beth H. Chaney; Michael L. Stellefson; Virginia Dodd
original_title: Validating the ability of a single-item assessing drunkenness to detect hazardous drinking
original_journal: The American Journal of Drug and Alcohol Abuse
replication_authors: Beth H. Chaney; Adam E. Barry; Jennifer Cremeens-Matthews; Ryan J. Martin; Michael L. Stellefson; Karen Vail-Smith
replication_title: Psychometric properties of a single-item assessing drunkenness to identify hazardous drinking: a replication study
explanation: The authors explicitly state 'Given that these study results support the findings of the initial study, it appears the non-quantity-based measure assessing drunkenness...could provide a valid, easy to administer, and brief measure.' The replication used the same methodology in a different geographic region with a different sample population.

description: Practicing nurses in the USA have significant knowledge deficits regarding the biophysiological and psychosocial components of alcohol and its pharmacological effects, and lack skill in identifying patients at risk for alcoholism
original_authors: Long P.; Gelfand G.
original_title: Alcohol education as primary prevention in health care
replication_authors: Perrin H. Long; G. Gelfand
replication_title: Alcohol education as primary prevention in health care: A replication study
explanation: The authors explicitly state they replicated their 1992 USA study in South Africa using the same questionnaire instrument with South African nurses. The Discussion states 'The findings of this study conducted in South Africa are similar to the findings of the earlier research done in the USA,' confirming successful replication of the core finding (nurses have substantial knowledge deficits about alcohol).

description: Exposure to electromagnetic radiation from a 2.4-GHz cordless phone base station causes measurable changes in heart rate variability (HRV) in human subjects, consistent with an autonomic nervous system stress response
original_authors: Havas, Magda; Marrongelle, Jeffrey; Pollner, Bernard; Kelley, Elizabeth; Rees, Camilla R.G.; Tully, Lizabeth
original_title: Provocation study using heart rate variability shows microwave radiation from 2.4 GHz cordless phone affects autonomic nervous system
replication_authors: Magda Havas; Jeffrey Marrongelle
replication_title: RETRACTED: Replication of heart rate variability provocation study with 2.4-GHz cordless phone confirms original findings
explanation: The title explicitly states 'confirms original findings' and the abstract calls this 'a replication of a study that we previously conducted in Colorado.' The same protocol (2.4-GHz cordless phone HRV provocation) was used with a larger sample (69 vs 25) across multiple sites, finding similar patterns of electrohypersensitivity. Classified as direct replication since the methodology is identical and differences (larger sample, different locations) are minor unavoidable variations. Confidence kept at medium because this paper was retracted in 2014, casting doubt on the reliability of both the original and replication results. The original study (Havas et al., 2010) was published in European Journal of Oncology and is a self-replication by the same lead authors.

description: Polymorphisms in the CXCR1 (interleukin-8 receptor alpha) gene are associated with susceptibility to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma in a German cohort

explanation: Reviewer verification: The result classification of 'failure' is unambiguous. The authors explicitly aimed 'to replicate previous findings that associated variants in these genes with COPD susceptibility' (referring to Stemmler et al. 2005, who found CXCR1 polymorphisms significantly associated with COPD in a German cohort). The replication clearly failed: 'we did not observed a significant effect of any IL-8, CXCR1 or CXCR2 polymorphism in the predisposition to COPD.' All odds ratios in Table 2 have 95% CIs crossing 1.0 with all p-values >0.05, and haplotype analyses were similarly non-significant. The authors acknowledge this explicitly in the Discussion: 'In our study no association was found between either of the two CXCR1 and CXCR2 genes variants and COPD risk susceptibility.' explanation: The authors document numerous coding errors in the original CDGLM study (wrong education variable, wrong child age cut-offs, incorrect age dummy simulation, comparison of different discount rates) and show that when corrected, all three headline findings are wrong: the effects of second/third children on forgone earnings are much larger than reported (25-30% vs 4-5%), education level differences are stronger, and the apparent large decline in forgone earnings since 1986 is explained by methodological errors. The authors conclude: 'We can show that all three headline features of the CDGLM results are mistaken.'

explanation: The replication found the opposite pattern: contextual learning outperformed translation pairs on gapped sentence tasks (F(2,1000)=6.2, p=.002, eta²=.01), with no significant advantage for translation pairs on any measure. The authors conclude: 'Our findings indicated that students who studied new vocabulary in context could perform as well as those who used translation on immediate posttests involving gapped sentences and translation' and the findings 'do not support the contention that switching to L1 in EFL classes to introduce new vocabulary is justified.'

explanation: The replication found both similarities and differences compared to the original. While most English teachers in Turkey also held positive perceptions about homework (similarity), unlike the original study teachers, they did not fully disregard the negative aspects of homework and their views on homework efficacy and student achievement varied and differed from the original study's teachers.

description: Common SNP variants within SORT1, CILP2/PBX4, APOE, LDL receptor, APOB, PCSK9, and HMGCoA reductase genes affect plasma LDL-cholesterol concentrations, as identified by genome-wide association studies

replication_authors: Hubacek JA; Adamkova V.; Lanska V.; Dlouha D.
replication_title: Polygenic Hypercholesterolemia: Examples of GWAS Results and Their Replication in the Czech-Slavonic Population
explanation: Independent review confirms 'inconclusive' is the appropriate classification for this genuinely mixed replication. The authors tested 7 gene loci (8 SNPs) from 4 GWAS papers (Kathiresan et al. 2008, Sandhu et al. 2008, Willer et al. 2008, Chasman et al. 2008) in 2,559 Czech-Slavonic adults. Five of 7 loci showed significant associations with LDL-cholesterol (SORT1, CILP2/PBX4, APOB rs693, APOE, LDL-R), but two did not (PCSK9 and HMGCoA reductase). The authors frame results positively — the Conclusion states 'We confirmed strong significant effects' and the Discussion opens with 'we geographically extended the validity' — but they also acknowledge the failures explicitly. For PCSK9, low frequency of the CC genotype (~3%) may explain the null result (power issue). For HMGCoA reductase, effect sizes were near zero (<0.09 mmol/l) across all genetic models, suggesting a genuine non-replication rather than a power issue. Because 5/7 loci replicated but 2 did not (with one likely a true negative), this is a genuinely mixed outcome. Confidence remains 'medium' because reasonable reviewers could classify this as 'success' (majority replicated, authors frame it positively) or 'inconclusive' (non-trivial failure rate). The ambiguity is inherent to the mixed-result pattern, not resolvable by closer reading.

explanation: The original study found that bilinguals and trilinguals showed significantly faster conflict resolution than monolinguals (and marginally so than L2 learners) in the Simon task (Experiment 1). In the replication, the Simon task yielded no significant differences between multilingual and L2 learner groups (F(1,156) < 1.5, p = 0.23), and Bayes factor analysis showed moderate evidence for the null hypothesis (BF10 = 0.28). The authors state: 'the Simon task data yielded no difference between groups, with multilinguals and monolinguals performing similarly.'

replication_authors: Gregory J. Poarch
replication_title: Multilingual Language Control and Executive Function: A Replication Study
explanation: The original study found that bilinguals and trilinguals outperformed L2 learners in resolving conflict in the Flanker-type task. In the replication, the Flanker task showed multilinguals exhibiting significantly smaller difference scores (55 ms) compared to L2 learners (85 ms), F(1,157) = 12.19, p < 0.001, with Bayes factor analysis showing very strong evidence for the alternative hypothesis (BF10 = 41.22). The authors state: 'the Flanker results corroborate the earlier findings.'

description: The MS4A2 -109T>C polymorphism (rs573790) is associated with susceptibility to aspirin-intolerant asthma/AERD in Korean patients
original_authors: Kim SH; Bae JS; Holloway JW; Lee JT; Suh CH; Nahm DH; Park HS
original_title: A polymorphism of MS4A2 (-109T > C) encoding the beta-chain of the high-affinity immunoglobulin E receptor (FcepsilonR1beta) is associated with a susceptibility to aspirin-intolerant asthma
replication_authors: Gandhi F. Pavón-Romero; Gloria Pérez-Rubio; Fernando Ramírez-Jiménez; Enrique Ambrocio-Ortiz; Elisé Bañuelos-Ortiz; Norma Alvarado-Franco; Karen E. Xochipa-Ruiz; Elizabeth Hernández-Juárez; Beatriz A. Flores-García; Ángel E. Camarena; Luis M. Terán; Ramcés Falfán-Valencia
replication_title: MS4A2-rs573790 Is Associated With Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease: Replicative Study Using a Candidate Gene Strategy
explanation: Independent review confirms 'success' classification. The paper is an explicit two-stage replicative study of candidate SNPs previously reported in other populations, tested in Mexican Mestizo patients. MS4A2-rs573790 (-109T>C, originally reported by Kim et al. 2006 in Koreans) was the only SNP significant in both stages. Stage 2 validation showed p=0.008 for AERD vs. healthy controls (co-dominant model) and p=0.03 (recessive model). The authors state unambiguously: 'rs573790 in the MS4A2 gene is the only SNP that supports an association with AERD in Mexican Mestizo patients in both stages of the study.' Replication type is 'close extension' because the same SNP-disease association is tested in a different ethnic population (Mexican Mestizo vs. Korean) using different genotyping methodology, which constitutes a meaningful extension of the original finding. Upgraded from medium to high confidence because the paper's conclusion is clear and unambiguous, with consistent statistical support across both study stages.
